analysis: Both units are base_text of docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (lines 1-422). No patch or head text was supplied, so the actual PR delta is not visible and this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. I read the base doc against T-041/SEC-035 and TB-007. Its stated cache posture matches the T-041 definition: HMAC lookup tags (SSDLookupKeys), DBK3 AES-GCM with an SE-rooted KEK, defaultTTL=maxTTL=1800s, a disk budget of half the free space with a 20 GiB fallback, a 20 GiB low-disk write stop, a rolling-day write ledger kept on the Mac, and CacheVolume.inspect and UUID pinning for external volumes. Doc-level claims in base that a later pass should check against the head diff: (1) the TTL cap of 1800s and the sign-off requirement for raising it (line 276); (2) the 'disk observer sees only lookup tag, weight hash, epoch, shape descriptors, createdAt' claim (line 77), plus the complete-checkpoint manifest, whose token IDs and tenant scope sit inside encrypted chunk 0 (lines 105-111); (3) per-file removals not rotating the epoch (lines 212 and 279); (4) the 'demand gate' for complete-checkpoint writes, which uses coordinator-supplied cache_repeated_prefix_tokens and a local 4096-entry tag history (line 278) and could widen the at-rest surface or timing oracle if changed; (5) the FIFO and O_NONBLOCK hardening (lines 68-75). If the head diff changes any of these values or claims without a matching T-041 or SEC-035 update, that should be flagged. The next pass should obtain the actual diff hunks.
